arm_a_answer:
For Viña del Sol I would recommend competitive benchmarking against its two direct Chilean rivals.

Internal benchmarking is cheapest and the data is already in-house, but the margin has been sliding for two years, so measuring the company against its own history only confirms the trend rather than showing what good looks like. The board asked for root causes; that won't give them any.

Functional benchmarking against the wider Latin American processing industry is a fairer comparison, but the product mix and scale differences would have to be normalised before any of the numbers meant anything, and that is a longer exercise than a board wanting answers this quarter will sit through.

Competitive benchmarking is the right call because the two rivals sell into the same market and work under the same Chilean food regulations, so any gap between them and Viña del Sol has to come from how the business is run rather than from circumstances management cannot control.

Viña del Sol's own gross margin has fallen from 38% to 31%, and on-time delivery is down to 74% against its 90% internal target. I would pull the two rivals' published margin and delivery figures and set them against those.
arm_b_answer:
Before choosing a method I would establish whether this is an operational problem at all. Gross margin has fallen from 38% to 31%, but if input costs across Chilean fruit processing have risen over the same two years, the whole sector's margins have moved and we would be benchmarking ourselves against a decline we share rather than one we caused. That test comes first, because it changes what the programme is for.

On the methods: internal benchmarking gives us a baseline and can isolate whether the 74% on-time delivery rate is concentrated in cold-press extraction or in aseptic filling, but it cannot tell us what good looks like.

Competitive benchmarking against the two Chilean rivals is the most relevant comparison and the least available one — both are privately held and publish nothing — so I would not build the programme on it. I would run it only in the limited form open to us: price comparisons, customer feedback and trade-association data.

Functional benchmarking is the primary external method. Cold-press extraction and aseptic filling are standard across Latin American processing, so best-in-class process data is genuinely obtainable.

Recommendation: internal to diagnose, functional to set targets, competitive as intelligence only.
